intro: You are walking into Laodicea, an ancient city in Denizli province, founded in the 3rd century BC. This was a wealthy trading city of the Lycus valley, with two theatres and broad avenues.
history: The Seleucid king Antiochus II founded the city for his wife Laodice. It grew rich on textiles and banking, and it was home to one of the Seven Churches.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss Syria Street, the West Theatre, the Laodicea Church and the water distribution terminal.
facts: Did you know? After the earthquake of AD 60, the city refused Roman aid and rebuilt itself with its own money — a detail Tacitus thought worth recording. Laodicea was one of the seven churches of Revelation. Its rebuke, 'neither cold nor hot', is thought to play on the water that arrived lukewarm through kilometres of aqueduct. And the city had two theatres, a stadium, and one of the largest ancient water-distribution terminals in Anatolia.
outro: This brings our tour of Laodicea to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This city once rebuilt itself by its own hand; let its stones stand for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
